note: Raw Phase 3B instrument layer. Instruments, targets and falsification tests only. Contains NO interview data and NO synthetic output. Regenerated - do not hand-edit.

banks.name: Current workflow
spec_questions: How do you currently track startups?
Where is startup data stored?
How do you manage mentors?
How do you track incubation milestones?
How do you manage IPR?
How do you generate reports?
How do you track student innovation?
What software do you currently use?
banks.rationale: This bank is the whole point of the phase. Phase 1's P-A10 says institution-wide innovation data is consolidated by hand, but we have only ever seen the EXPORT - never the tool upstream of it. Every question here is anchored to the last completed cycle, not to the general present.

banks.name: Pain
spec_questions: What takes the most time?
What gets missed?
What information is difficult to obtain?
What do you currently do manually?
What causes reporting problems?
What information do you wish you had in one dashboard?
banks.rationale: Anchored to the last submission cycle. 'What takes the most time' is unusable without a timeframe; the reframed form asks for hours spent on the last cycle, which is answerable.

banks.name: Existing tools
spec_questions: What software do you currently pay for?
What is free?
What do you use Excel for?
What do you use WhatsApp for?
What systems does the institution already have?
banks.rationale: This is the bank that tests the 'free incumbent' assumption underpinning StartupHub's entire pricing model. Phase 0 assumes Excel / Sheets / WhatsApp are free incumbents. That is currently an ASSUMPTION, not a finding.

banks.name: Buying
spec_questions: Who approves new software?
Who controls the budget?
How long does procurement take?
What budget category would this fall under?
What would prevent you from buying it?
banks.rationale: Phase 2 proved only 4 of 25 roles hold DOCUMENTED budget authority, and none is Class A. This bank is the only way to find out whether that documentary finding matches reality - and whether the person we interview can even authorise anything.

banks.name: Value
spec_questions: If this problem disappeared tomorrow, what would that save you?
banks.rationale: todo.md is explicit that this is the right question and 'would you pay Rs 1.2 lakh' is the wrong one. It is reframed here to demand a quantity - hours, or rupees already committed - because 'it would save a lot of time' is not evidence.

guides.title: IIC Convener / Coordinator / ARIIA-NIRF nodal officer
guides.why_first: Phase 1 shows this is one part-time academic doing the work for the whole institution (SSCET: 40 IIC members, 30 ambassadors, 2 mentors; NIT Calicut: 29 mentors against 155 ideas). They are simultaneously the user, the evidence source, and the only plausible internal champion. They are also the person who already discovered the DPIIT join problem in practice.

questions.q: Walk me through the last NIRF innovation submission you filed, start to finish. Where did you begin?
questions.probe: What was open on your screen? What was next to it?
questions.falsifies: If they begin from a single system that already holds a venture list, the 'no venture register' gap is smaller than Phase 1 concluded.

questions.q: In that same submission, you had to record a TRL for each innovation. Where did the DPIIT registration number come from?
questions.probe: Did you ask the founder? Look it up on the DPIIT portal? Did someone else give you a list?
questions.falsifies: Resolves OQ-32. Determines whether the product is a better spreadsheet or a workflow carrier.

questions.q: When you could not find a DPIIT number for a startup, what did you actually type into the cell?
questions.probe: Did you leave it blank, put a placeholder, or drop the row entirely?
questions.falsifies: Explains the DIPP0000 placeholders in 3 real forms.

questions.q: How long did that whole submission take you, and how much of it was re-work?
questions.probe: Roughly how many hours? Was there a point where you had to redo rows?
questions.falsifies: P-A08 grades hand-assembly DOCUMENTED; this tests whether it is felt as rework.

questions.q: What do you use between cycles to keep track of these startups - before the form asks you to?
questions.probe: Excel? Google Sheets? WhatsApp groups? A register someone else maintains?
questions.falsifies: P-A01 asks whether institutions keep a venture register at all.

questions.q: Is that spreadsheet yours, or does it come from someone else in the institute?
questions.probe: Who else edits it? Does the Registrar see it?
questions.falsifies: Tests whether Convener and Incubation Manager are one person, and whether data flows upward.

questions.q: When ARIIA asks for a similar count a few weeks later, do you reuse the same list?
questions.probe: Have you ever compared the two numbers?
questions.falsifies: If they reuse and reconcile, the duplication problem is weaker than claimed.

questions.q: You asked for Rs 1.2 lakh for something. Where did that number come from?
questions.probe: Did you compare it to something you already spend, or was it a guess?
questions.falsifies: Tests whether the price band is anchored to anything real.

guides.title: Registrar / Dean (ICSR) / Controller of Examinations-adjacent office
guides.why_first: Phase 2's only role with DOCUMENTED budget authority in Class C. Interviewing them at the SAME institution as the Convener is the entire point: two accounts of one portfolio that can be compared line by line.

questions.q: Does the institute's official record of startups come to you, or do you go and get it?
questions.probe: Who compiles it? How often? In what format?
questions.falsifies: P-A10 documents consolidation by hand; this tests who owns the output.

questions.q: Last time an annual report or NIRF filing needed innovation numbers, what did you do with them?
questions.probe: Did you chase anyone? Did you get them once or repeatedly?
questions.falsifies: P-A04 says one coordinator is the integration point for several problems.

questions.q: Which budget head would a Rs 1-2 lakh annual software purchase come from?
questions.probe: Have you approved anything in this range? Under which head?
questions.falsifies: OQ-29 asks exactly this. Phase 0 has no answer.

questions.q: Walk me through the last software purchase you approved. What was the route?
questions.probe: Was there a committee? GeM? Direct purchase? How many weeks?
questions.falsifies: Tests whether the Rs 50K-Rs 10L committee spread is reality.

questions.q: What would make you NOT approve this?
questions.probe: Is there a security questionnaire? A data-localisation clause?
questions.falsifies: OQ-30 asks whether IT Admin has a veto.

questions.q: Is there an existing system that already holds this, and why wasn't it used?
questions.probe: ERP? Student information system? Existing software renewal?
questions.falsifies: If a paid system already exists, the incumbent is not free.

guides.title: Purchase Committee member / IT Administrator / Finance officer
guides.why_first: They control the money and the security gate but do not do the work, so workflow questions are wasted slots. Phase 2 found the IT Administrator appears in ZERO procurement instruments by name.

questions.q: What falls below a committee, and what goes to it?
questions.probe: Is there a de-minimis threshold? Has it changed?
questions.falsifies: Confirms or breaks the documented Rs 50K-Rs 10L spread.

questions.q: If a vendor must store venture data on their own servers, who signs that off?
questions.probe: Has anyone ever refused a purchase on security grounds?
questions.falsifies: Resolves whether IT Admin has a real veto.

questions.q: What security documents do you require from a software vendor?
questions.probe: SOC 2? ISO 27001? Data localisation? Government cloud only?
questions.falsifies: Tests whether on-premise/data-localisation is universal.

guides.title: Student founder / incubator participant
guides.why_first: They are the source of the DPIIT number and the person who experiences the missing record, but they cannot buy anything. The buying bank is skipped to protect interview time.

questions.q: After your startup was recognised, did anyone at the institute ask you for anything - a form, a number, a report?
questions.probe: Did you get asked for your DPIIT number? Did you have to dig for it?
questions.falsifies: Tests the founder side of the join-key problem.

questions.q: Is there any place you can see what stage your own startup is at, that the institute also sees?
questions.probe: Or is it only the institute that tracks it?
questions.falsifies: P-A06 grades stock-not-movement DOCUMENTED.

questions.q: When your institute filed a report that mentioned you, did it get anything wrong?
questions.probe: Did you correct it? Did anyone notice?
questions.falsifies: Tests whether the ledger is wrong about real startups.

questions.q: What do you personally use to keep track of your startup right now?
questions.probe: Notes app? WhatsApp? Google Sheets? Nothing?
questions.falsifies: Tests the 'free incumbent' claim from the user side.

hypotheses.claim: Institutions have no venture register; StartupHub's portfolio is the first.
hypotheses.refuting_observation: A Convener opens an existing system - institute ERP, a student information system, or a maintained shared sheet - that already lists their startups with names, stages and dates.
hypotheses.if_refuted: The wedge is 'one place to see it', not 'first record'. Pricing and moat both weaken.

hypotheses.claim: IPR tracking is a real institutional problem, not just a documentation gap.
hypotheses.source: P-A07 DOCUMENTED CRITICAL - no institution has a patent deadline calendar
hypotheses.refuting_observation: IPR is handled by an outside agency or a TTO, deadlines are tracked on individual researchers' own systems, and the institute itself never tracks a patent.
hypotheses.if_refuted: The CRITICAL finding is a reporting artefact. The patent module loses its justification.

interview.title: IIC Convener / Coordinator / ARIIA-NIRF nodal officer
interview.why_first: Phase 1 shows this is one part-time academic doing the work for the whole institution (SSCET: 40 IIC members, 30 ambassadors, 2 mentors; NIT Calicut: 29 mentors against 155 ideas). They are simultaneously the user, the evidence source, and the only plausible internal champion. They are also the person who already discovered the DPIIT join problem in practice.

questions.q: Walk me through the last NIRF innovation submission you filed, start to finish. Where did you begin?
questions.probe: What was open on your screen? What was next to it?
questions.falsifies: If they begin from a single system that already holds a venture list, the 'no venture register' gap is smaller than Phase 1 concluded.

hypotheses.claim: On-premise / data-localisation is a near-universal procurement condition.
hypotheses.refuting_observation: A cloud SaaS product with no on-premise option clears procurement without objection, because the data is non-sensitive.
hypotheses.if_refuted: The deployment constraint is soft and the vendor list narrows sharply.

interview.title: Purchase Committee member / IT Administrator / Finance officer
interview.why_first: They control the money and the security gate but do not do the work, so workflow questions are wasted slots. Phase 2 found the IT Administrator appears in ZERO procurement instruments by name.

questions.q: What falls below a committee, and what goes to it?
questions.probe: Is there a de-minimis threshold? Has it changed?
questions.falsifies: Confirms or breaks the documented Rs 50K-Rs 10L spread.

questions.q: If a vendor must store venture data on their own servers, who signs that off?
questions.probe: Has anyone ever refused a purchase on security grounds?
questions.falsifies: Resolves whether IT Admin has a real veto.

questions.q: What security documents do you require from a software vendor?
questions.probe: SOC 2? ISO 27001? Data localisation? Government cloud only?
questions.falsifies: Tests whether on-premise/data-localisation is universal.

shortlist.contradiction: 55 vs 17 startups in one PDF; Rs 1,51,488 vs Rs 16,00,000 awareness spend (P-A08)
shortlist.why: The single largest documented internal contradiction in the corpus. Both halves of that discrepancy were produced by the same office in the same document, so the Convener can explain it - or cannot, which is equally informative.

shortlist.contradiction: 6 startups recognised, TRL evidence for only 2 - the worst join rate measured (67%)
shortlist.why: The Phase 3A headline has a live example. Asking this officer directly where the other 4 DPIIT numbers went is the single highest-value question in the whole programme.

shortlist.contradiction: TRL table carries a DPIIT number absent from the recognised table (reverse gap)
shortlist.why: A contradiction in the opposite direction - the data exists but is filed under a key nobody recognised. Tests whether anyone reconciles the two tables (OQ-34).

shortlist.contradiction: A 13-item grant narrative inserted into a field meant for a number (P-A02)
shortlist.why: The most vivid evidence of form abuse in the corpus, and the officer who typed it can describe the pressure. Best case for H-04 - is the deadline actually forcing bad data?

shortlist.institution: Dr. N.G.P. Arts and Science College
shortlist.contradiction: Grant figure reconciles to two unrelated DBT grants - aggregation presented as one number (P-A09)
shortlist.why: Tests whether institutions can state what a rupee of government money actually funded. Directly probes the stock-vs-flow problem behind P-A06.

shortlist.contradiction: 40 IIC members, 30 ambassadors, 2 mentors - ratio implies capacity, not pipeline
shortlist.why: A high-volume institution with an implausibly thin mentoring base. Best case for testing H-08 (are cohorts real?) and H-03 (what is the 2-mentor process actually doing).

exclusions.reason: Its ARIIA records 0 IIC stars while running a mature incubator. Tempting, but the 0 is probably an officer who delegates the form - we would get the wrong respondent. Approach second, through a named coordinator.
Excellent documentary evidence, but a Convener there is unlikely to be doing the data work personally. We need people who touch the spreadsheet, not people who sign it.

consent: This is a research interview about how your institution handles startup and innovation records. It is not a sales call and not a product demo.
We will not share anything you tell us with other institutions, or name your institution in any external material without asking you first.
We may quote you anonymously, attributed only to your role and institution type (for example 'a Convener at a central university'), unless you ask us not to.
You may skip any question, or stop the interview at any point, with no consequence.
We are recording notes and, with your permission, audio, purely so we do not misquote you.
There is no payment. If you would like a summary of what we learn, we will send it.

analysis_rules: One interview is an anecdote. No code may be reported as a finding until it appears in at least 3 of 6 institutions, and the count of institutions is always printed beside it.
A claim that contradicts Phase 1 or 3A is recorded as a contradiction, never silently dropped. Phase 1's corpus is evidence too.
Paired interviews are compared on the same four questions: does the Registrar's picture match the Convener's, on venture count, on who owns the data, and on what was last paid for.
Silence is recorded. If a respondent cannot answer a question, that is a coded non-answer and counts toward the finding - an institution that cannot name its own budget head is the finding.
Quotes are verbatim only, with the recording checked. No paraphrase is ever placed in quotation marks.
Every finding states which hypotheses it confirms, refutes, or leaves open. An interview that resolves nothing is still recorded, and still costs time - say so.

ollama_rules.purpose: Validate that the interview guides are answerable and non-leading BEFORE a human is asked them. A synthetic respondent should produce an answer that is obviously synthesised and reveals nothing real.
forbidden: any synthetic text entering _exports/ (except _exports/synthetic/, which is excluded from the manifest)
any synthetic sentence being quoted as a respondent
any synthetic count entering a finding, grade, or headline
a synthetic answer being used to 'confirm' a hypothesis
recording synthetic output with a parse_status of 'parsed'
ollama_rules.instruction: Run a synthetic respondent against each guide with a deliberately wrong, inconsistent persona, to check the questions do not lead the answer. A model that answers everything smoothly means the question is leading.
